Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] The class's carried-forward build, with the one part of 3.2.0 that actually concerns Paladin bolted on. The PTR gives Paladin the +30% core-stat scalar (1.25 to 1.625) and a set of Holy-line adjustments - Holy Bolt, Blessed Shield, and a redesigned Judgement - and the digest's summary is 'surprisingly few changes' with set balance still unaddressed. The base build touches none of the Holy line: Shield Charge, Clash, Condemn, Fortress and the two auras are not mentioned in the 3.2.0 notes at all. That is a comfortable position and also a wasteful one, because it means the build collects exactly one of the patch's two gifts. This variant keeps the whole Thorns and block engine and puts Blessed Shield in Condemn's bar slot as a ranged filler, so the Holy-line changes have somewhere to land. Strength rises in the affix priorities for the scalar. Both aggregator class lists put Paladin at B, unchanged from live, and nothing here disputes that.

Rotation
  1. Auras up, Clash on cooldown for Resolve, Shield Charge through the middle of the pack so the hits count as blocks, then Blessed Shield at anything the charge did not reach.
Variants

Leveling — [ptr] Auras up, Clash for Resolve, Shield Charge through the pack so hits count as blocks and Retribution pulses.
Move on when Herald of Zakarum equipped - or level 70 from Mrak on the PTR.

Early Endgame — [ptr] Auras up, Clash on cooldown, Shield Charge through the pack, Blessed Shield at anything the charge did not reach. That last clause is the whole variant.
Move on when Maximum Resolve at 30 and block chance climbing.

Late Endgame — [ptr] Same loop. Aspect of Interdiction should be pushing block chance toward the 100% threshold by now.
Move on when 100% block chance, which activates Aspect of Redirected Force.

Pushing — [ptr] Untested on 3.2.0. The Holy-line changes are described without numbers in every source available, so the value of the Blessed Shield slot is genuinely unknown - measure it against Condemn before committing to it in a push.

Uniques
  • chest [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: Harbinger of Hatred, Nahantu near the Kurast Docks waypoint; 1x Greater Lair Key from the Initiate lair bosses. Where →
  • offhand [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: Astaroth, at the end of Escalating Nightmare Dungeons, Torment 1+; 1x Escalation Sigil. Where →
  • pants [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: General Unique Pool from any lair boss, plus vendor gambling. Where →
  • amulet [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: General Unique Pool or Horadric Cube - and note 3.2.0's Mythic crafting rework offers three routes, two of which bypass the one-Crafted-Mythic cap. Where →

How to run them

[ptr] Carried over from Season 14 unchanged: the official 3.2.0 notes do not mention mercenaries at all. Identical across all four variants: hire Raheir, who 'grants you Bastion and Inspiration to buff your damage', and reinforce with Aldkin, who 'reduces enemy damage and slows with Field of Languish'. Note this is the opposite emphasis from most Season 14 builds, which take Raheir purely for survivability - here Inspiration is picked up as a damage node, which is the tell that this build already has its own defence covered by block, Resolve and Fortress and is spending the mercenary slot on offence and on the damage-reduction layer instead.

Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] The class's carried-forward build, with the one part of 3.2.0 that actually concerns Paladin bolted on. The PTR gives Paladin the +30% core-stat scalar (1.25 to 1.625) and a set of Holy-line adjustments - Holy Bolt, Blessed Shield, and a redesigned Judgement - and the digest's summary is 'surprisingly few changes' with set balance still unaddressed. The base build touches none of the Holy line: Shield Charge, Clash, Condemn, Fortress and the two auras are not mentioned in the 3.2.0 notes at all. That is a comfortable position and also a wasteful one, because it means the build collects exactly one of the patch's two gifts. This variant keeps the whole Thorns and block engine and puts Blessed Shield in Condemn's bar slot as a ranged filler, so the Holy-line changes have somewhere to land. Strength rises in the affix priorities for the scalar. Both aggregator class lists put Paladin at B, unchanged from live, and nothing here disputes that.

Rotation
  1. Auras up, Clash on cooldown for Resolve, Shield Charge through the middle of the pack so the hits count as blocks, then Blessed Shield at anything the charge did not reach.
Variants

Leveling — [ptr] Auras up, Clash for Resolve, Shield Charge through the pack so hits count as blocks and Retribution pulses.
Move on when Herald of Zakarum equipped - or level 70 from Mrak on the PTR.

Early Endgame — [ptr] Auras up, Clash on cooldown, Shield Charge through the pack, Blessed Shield at anything the charge did not reach. That last clause is the whole variant.
Move on when Maximum Resolve at 30 and block chance climbing.

Late Endgame — [ptr] Same loop. Aspect of Interdiction should be pushing block chance toward the 100% threshold by now.
Move on when 100% block chance, which activates Aspect of Redirected Force.

Pushing — [ptr] Untested on 3.2.0. The Holy-line changes are described without numbers in every source available, so the value of the Blessed Shield slot is genuinely unknown - measure it against Condemn before committing to it in a push.

Reasoning

Based onShield Charge Thorns Paladin
Tweaks vs. the base build
  1. [ptr] Blessed Shield replaces Condemn on the bar from the early endgame. Condemn is a gathering tool the base build takes at one point; Blessed Shield is one of the three Holy skills 3.2.0 actually adjusts and it is a ranged Thorns delivery, which the base build has none of.
  2. [ptr] Strength rises in the helm, weapon and ring priorities. The core-stat scalar going 1.25 to 1.625 is a flat 30% on baseline damage per 10 Strength and it is the one unambiguous gain in the patch for this class.
  3. [ptr] Nothing is built around a set. The digest is explicit that set balance is still unaddressed on 3.2.0, so the Phoba of Righteous Will charm set is kept for the Maximum Resolve it provides - which is arithmetic the Resolve cap needs - rather than for a set bonus.
  4. [ptr] Resolve capping to 30 is unchanged and still matters: three +6 Maximum Resolve tempers, Aspect of Glynn's Anvil and the charm set. 3.2.0 does not touch Resolve, Retribution or the auras.
  5. [ptr] Soul Splinter: Splinter of Pain, for the Damage Reduction at the cost of -30% Movement Speed. A Thorns build wants to be hit and does not want to be anywhere in particular, so the drawback is close to free here - which is unusual and worth saying. Splinter of Anguish is the alternative if your critical strike chance is high enough to convert it; the base guide's own rule is that critical strike damage is worth more the more critical strike chance you have and less when you have little.
  6. [ptr] No War Plans: 3.2.0 changes nothing about the system and no per-build picks exist for any season.
